summary: During the High Court dispute over coalition-related budget transfers approved in election recess, Smotrich conveyed an all-or-none position opposing separation of urgent spending from the disputed package; the court instead required urgent items to be separated. On Aug. 24 the High Court narrowed the freeze to NIS 409 million in identified coalition transfers, released urgent transfers, and issued a conditional order requiring respondents to explain why the coalition transfers should not be canceled.
notes: This run adds independent Jerusalem Post corroboration of the Aug. 24 procedural outcome. The reporting strengthens the litigation history but still does not by itself establish a qualifying personal accountability finding against Smotrich, nor did this pass recover the primary High Court order/case number. Preserve Pending; do not characterize the transfers as finally unlawful or infer motive.
